title: Draygar WarSmash
type: Player character · warrior, rescuer, and champion against Wrath
dek: A smith and frontline companion whose strength becomes an offer of work, a wager for a friend, a confession to Gartina and an argument for justice within the Silver Star.

body:
Draygar brings a smith’s habits into the company: look for what can be used, offer strong hands, keep the equipment ready and stand where someone else needs room to survive. His courage can run ahead of safety, but his history also records listening, needing help and trying to protect friends through more than force.

October 2024 · strength used practically

Early scenes establish that Draygar can survive punishment without being invulnerable. He rescues fallen companions, calls for medical help, and uses his body as transport and cover rather than treating endurance as permission to ignore risk. His endurance helps him bring injured companions home.

Faith learned through need and action

Early in his service, Draygar prays to Cala while admitting that she does not know him. Krone has told him she is a good goddess, and his companions need help. The relationship begins in the recovered scenes with trust borrowed from a friend and a request made under danger.

He later thanks Cala for a mace. By the confrontation after Wrath’s fall he holds a radiant warhammer and explicitly calls it her gift. The scenes do not establish that every named weapon is the same object or recover the complete terms of the bond.

What he does with the gift is clearer. He is willing to put it forward when he asks Death to restore Olokun. Faith does not mean keeping the weapon untouched by his own judgment; it becomes something he is prepared to risk for a person.

The assault on Wrath · an offer Death refuses

After Saray kills Wrath, Draygar picks up the fallen sword and throws it at Death, accusing him of bringing only death despite his talk of a beautiful world. Later, when Death refuses to give the company weapons it could use against him, Draygar proposes a trade. He holds up Cala’s radiant warhammer and asks for Olokun’s return. Saray offers her own possessions; Krone holds out his maul and asks for his new family back. Death rejects objects in exchange for souls and closes the door. Draygar answers, “Well.... Ay tried.” The exchange ends without an accepted bargain or the hammer changing hands.

The person beyond the cooking

Food gives Draygar reasons to stay near Gartina, but he eventually says it was never the whole reason. During the dragon battle in the Month of Cala, Year 2, badly burned and hurt, he tells her that she caught his eye at the Tower and that he ate more than he needed to remain with her a little longer.

He speaks as though he may not have another chance, then turns toward the danger again. The confession establishes his feelings at that moment; it does not claim that he dies there or supply a complete account of when their relationship began.

Later they arrive at public gatherings together. He consults her, notices her reactions and calls her his love. Ordinary things—food, work in a shared kitchen, a kiss before she speaks—sit beside the fear of losing someone in battle.

Gartina can also change what he does. In the leadership gathering she helps turn his support toward Wren. Love is present in a decision about the wider community, not only in an isolated domestic future. Marriage, a complete household history and every later choice remain unestablished.

The danger inside strength

Draygar’s willingness to go first can leave him hurt and relying on companions. At the Citadel he accepts Wren’s potions and waits while others make the passage safe. Anger and strength do not win his friends back from Death; he still has to decide what to do next. His work includes rescue, carrying information and consulting Gartina, alongside fights he cannot settle by hitting harder.

The memorial later tests that duty again. Holding up the hammer in Cala’s light, Draygar calls for Elenia to bring Magnus back and end the conflict. When Magnus returns, he offers water and asks him to breathe. He can oppose a person’s argument and still attend to the vulnerable person in front of him.

Open record

Draygar’s life before the early Pristinia scenes, the exact origins and rules of his bond with Cala, the complete history of the hammer, the beginning of his relationship with Gartina and his later fate remain incompletely recovered. His remembered mountain home adds a personal glimpse without establishing a named birthplace.

Contemporary reputation · 15 July and 30 August 2025

Ada first remembers Draygar beside Krone—the force that holds beside the force that advances—then emphasizes Draygar’s ability to calm conflict, support grieving companions, and prevent despair from becoming violence. The public record therefore remembers emotional steadiness alongside martial strength. Read the chronicler’s evidence boundary.

A forge and the Silver Star

Draygar greets the gift of the castle with delight in its stonework and a wish to put his cot beside the forge. He tells Elenia and Olokun that he intends to join the Silver Star. He also describes his connection to his ancestors and says the place gives him a sense of wonder and danger. These are his impressions and plans, rather than proof of an unseen local threat or a completed initiation.

The Citadel · making room for other people’s skills

Before the company reaches Wrath, Draygar calls for people to spread out and tells companions to disengage if they need someone else to take their place in the fight. He wants the enemy caster brought down, accepts Scribonia’s help in reaching him and angrily pursues him when he escapes. His instructions do not make him an unruffled commander; the same fight records impatience, laughter and wounds.

At the gate he urges everyone inside, drinks both potions Wren gave him and then stands back while people better suited to the task make a safe passage. A little later he accepts Bitoshi’s berries without counting them. His endurance depends on other people’s supplies and judgment as well as on his own willingness to advance. The full assault follows the company through the battle and the failed appeals afterward.

The smith who offers a pair of hands

In the early Pristinia scenes, Draygar arrives beside Krone, joking about ale and height, then tells Melian he is there to help the town get on its feet. If she needs strong hands, he says she can find him with Gareth or Jon.

His forge is already part of his life. He recognizes usable metal, thinks about salvage and later compares the heat of dangerous places with the work he knows. Calling Krone brother establishes intimacy and comradeship; these exchanges do not by themselves recover a biological genealogy.

He remembers a mountain home with lava, but its name and his whole life before Pristinia remain unresolved. The scenes first give him to the reader through work, jokes and an offer of help, rather than a reputation earned in a later battle.

A Silver Star member argues for his friends

After Aria’s death, Draygar stands before the grieving Zarathians as a member of the Silver Star. He asks for truth and justice while admitting the loss matters to their people. Rather than exile, he proposes work that would help the city recover and fill the absence Aria leaves.

His suspicion of Míriel is his reading of her words and manner. He cannot simply convert it into proof of every hidden motive. He stays to help with the procession, updates Gartina and wears the mourning dress he remembers from his dwarven home.

At the later leadership gathering he nominates Tyragol and offers to act as an adventurer ambassador. Neither proposal appoints him. When the Silver Star ultimately names Wren, he supports her, praising both her ability and her care for people. He also offers Magnus a steady ear and urges him to choose advisers who will help rather than use him.

His allegiance does not remove the need to judge. The smith who asks to join a meticulous craft tradition now argues about how that tradition should treat his friends. He wants to protect a community without giving up the people it mistrusts.

profile.personality: Draygar is boisterous, sociable, physically fearless, and frequently funny without being careless about other people’s danger. His strength is not an identity he hoards; it is a service he can offer. The same person who jokes about food and height immediately hauls fallen companions clear, calls for a medic, or puts an enormous body between danger and someone who cannot withstand it.
profile.achievements: Across Pristinia, Gael, The Before, and the campaign against Wrath, Draygar repeatedly uses his strength to rescue others. He carries the warhammer Cala, throws Wrath’s sword at Death and offers Cala’s hammer for Olokun’s return; Death rejects the proposed exchange. He earns Captain Zythienne’s promised recommendation to Captain Tarwen after the dragon-isle battle; this exchange alone does not establish formal Silver Star admission.
profile.relationships: Krone is his sworn brother and the clearest anchor of Draygar’s fellowship, while Gartina brings tenderness, trust, and the possibility of a life beyond the next battle into his record. Herb, Jon, Gareth, Melian, and many changing expedition parties know a man who makes belonging through food, ale, teasing, and immediate practical help. He is most fully himself when another person needs to be carried home.
